82:1: God Almighty says: When the sky is split open: it is split, and its stars are scattered from it and fall.
82:2: God Almighty says: And when the stars are scattered.
82:3: God Almighty says: And when the seas burst forth, meaning: God bursts some of them into others, filling them all. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the interpretation said, with some differences among them regarding some of that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when the seas burst forth, he said: some of them into others. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And when the seas burst forth, means the fresh water bursts forth into the salty water, and the salty water bursts into the fresh water. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan: And when the seas burst forth, he said: Some of them burst forth into others, and their water was lost. Al-Kalbi said: They were filled.
82:4: And his saying: And when the graves are scattered, meaning: And when the graves are stirred up, and the dead in them are extracted alive, it is said that someone scattered the pool of someone else: if he made its bottom its top, it is said: he scattered it and searched it, two languages. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when the graves are scattered, he said: searched.
82:5: And His statement: Every soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind. God Almighty says: Every soul will know what it has put forward for that day of righteous deeds that will benefit it, and what it has left behind of something that it has established and acted upon. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said about this. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, who told me on the authority of al-Qurazi that he said regarding A soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind, he said: What it has put forward of what it has done. As for what it has left behind, it is the Sunnah that a man sets for those who come after him to follow. Others said: What he meant by that is: what you have done of the obligatory prayers, and what you have delayed of the obligatory prayers, which you have neglected. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed bin Masruq, on the authority of Ikrimah: A soul will know what it has put forward He said: What was required of it. And what it has delayed He said: Of what was required of it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, A soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind. He said: It will know what it has put forward of obedience to God, and what it has left behind, what it was commanded to do of God’s right over it, but it did not act upon it. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, A soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind, he said: What it has put forward of good and what it has left behind of the right of God upon it, it has not acted upon it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: What I have done in the past and in the future He said: What I have done in the past of obedience to God and what I have done in the future of the right of God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Every soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind, he said: What it has put forward means what it has done, and what it has left behind means what it has neglected, wasted, and left behind of the righteous work to which God has called it. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: what you have done of good or evil, and what you have left behind of good or evil. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi, he said: This verse was mentioned to him: Every soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind. He said: I am among what Al-Hajjaj left behind. We chose the statement we mentioned because everything that the servant does, good or evil, is what he has done in the past, and whatever he has wasted of God’s right over him and neglected and not done, is what he has done in the past of evil, and that is not what he has delayed in the past of work, because the work is what he has done, but what he has not done is only a bad thing that he has done in the past. Therefore we said: what he has delayed is what he has established of good or bad practice, which if the worker does it he will have the same reward or burden as the one who does it.
82:6: God Almighty says: O disbelieving human being, what has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord? It is his enemy who has power over him who has deceived the human being, as: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, What has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord? Nothing has deceived the son of Adam, this enemy, Satan.
82:7: And His saying: Who created you and proportioned you means: He who created you, O human being, proportioned your creation and balanced you. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Mecca, Syria, and Basra recited it as fa-‘adlaka with a shaddah on the dal, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it without a shaddah. It is as if the one who recited it with a shaddah directed the meaning of the speech to that He made you moderate, of a balanced nature, and upright. It is as if the one who recited it without a shaddah directed the meaning of the speech to: He turned you and your hopes to whatever image He wanted, either to a good image, or to an ugly image, or to the image of some of His relatives. The first of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the most correct, to say: They are two readings known in the reading of the regions, correct in meaning, so whichever of them the reader reads is correct, except that what I like the most is the reading of the one who reads it with the shaddah, because the use of fi for modification is better in Arabic than its use for justice. Do you not see that you say: I treated you well in such-and-such, and turned you towards it, but you hardly ever say: I treated you well to such-and-such and turned you towards it? That is why I chose the shaddah. In a similar manner to what we said about that and mentioned that the readers of that interpreted it, the narration came from the people of interpretation that they said it.
82:8: The narration mentioned that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, In whatever form He willed, He has assembled you, he said: In any resemblance of a father or mother, maternal uncle or paternal uncle. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, regarding his statement, Whatever He wills, He wills you. He said: If He wills, He will ride you in the form of a dog, and if He wills, He will ride you in the form of a donkey. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih: In whatever form He wills, He will put you in. He said: A pig or a donkey. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, In whatever form He wills, He has put you together, he said: If He wills, in the form of a monkey, and if He wills, in the form of a pig. Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told me: Mutahhar ibn al-Haytham told us: Musa ibn Ali ibn Abi Rabah al-Lakhmi told us: My father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What child will you have? He said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what will be born to me? Either a boy or a girl. He said: Who will he resemble? He said: O Messenger of God, who will he resemble? Either his father or his mother. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Stop! Do not say that. When the sperm settles in the womb, God brings about every lineage between it and Adam. Have you not read this verse in the Book of God: In whatever form He wills He casts you. He said: He has put you in a thread.
82:9: God Almighty says: The matter, O disbelievers, is not as you say, that you are right in your worship of other than God, but you deny reward and punishment, recompense and accountability. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement, But you deny the Recompense, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Rather, you deny the Judgment, he said: the reckoning. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ both narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, You deny the Judgment, he said: the Day of Judgment. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Rather, you deny the Judgment, he said: A day of hardship, a day on which God will judge the servants according to their deeds.
82:10: And His statement: And over you are guardians, meaning: And over you are guardians who record your deeds and count them for you.
82:11: God Almighty says: Honorable scribes. He says: Honorable scribes before God, who write down your deeds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Some of our companions said, on the authority of Ayoub, regarding His statement, And over you are guardians, * noble and recording, he said: They write down what you say and what you mean.
82:12: And His statement: They know what you do means: These guardians know what you do, good or bad, and they record it against you.
82:13: And His saying: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss. God Almighty says: Indeed, those who were righteous by performing God’s obligations and avoiding His sins will be in the bliss of Paradise, enjoying themselves therein.
82:14: God Almighty says: And indeed, the wicked who disbelieved in their Lord will be in Hellfire.
82:15: And His statement: They will burn in it on the Day of Judgment, God Almighty says: These wicked people will burn in Hell on the Day of Resurrection, the day when the servants will be judged by their deeds and rewarded for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying The Day of Judgment is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. God has made it great and warned His servants about it.
82:16: And His statement: And they will not be absent from it means, the Most High said: These wicked people will never leave Hell and will be absent from it, but they will remain in it eternally, and so will the righteous in bliss, and this is similar to His statement: And they will not be removed from it (al-Hijr 15:48).
82:17: His statement: And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: What will make you know, O Muhammad? That is, what will make you aware of what the Day of Judgment is! He says: What is the Day of Reckoning and Recompense? He magnifies His status, may He be glorified, by saying that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is? is an emphasis on the Day of Resurrection, the day on which people will be judged by their deeds.
82:18: And his saying: Then what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is? He says: Then what will make you feel what the Day of Recompense and Reckoning is, O Muhammad! To magnify his matter.
82:19: Then He, the Most High, explained some of His status, saying: The Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul. He says: That is the Day, the Day when no soul will possess anything: He says: The Day when no soul will avail another soul at all, nor will it ward off a calamity that has befallen it, nor will it benefit it with anything beneficial. In this world, it used to protect it and ward off from it whoever sought to harm it, but that will be invalidated on that Day, because the matter will be for God, Whom no conqueror can overcome and no conqueror can subdue. There the kingdoms will be destroyed, the leadership will be lost, and the kingdom will belong to the Mighty King. That is His saying: And the matter on that Day will belong to God. He says: And the whole matter on that Day, meaning the religion, will belong to God, without the rest of His creation. No one of His creation will have a command or prohibition with Him on that Day. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the command on that Day will be God’s. He said: There will be no one on that Day who will decide anything except the Lord of the Worlds. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, On the Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul, and the command that Day will be God’s, and the command, by God, today is God’s, but on that day no one will dispute Him. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, The Day when no soul will possess power. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Kufa recited it with the accusative case of day, since its addition was not pure. Some of the reciters of Basra recited it with the damma of day and its nominative case in response to the first day. The nominative case is more eloquent in the speech of the Arabs, because the day is added to yaf’ala, and when the Arabs add the day to tafa’ala, “yaf’ala,” or af’ala, they raise it and say, This is the day when I will do such-and-such. If they add it to a past tense verb, they lower it. From this is the saying of the poet: While I blamed gray hair for my youth and said, Didn’t you recover while gray hair is a deterrent?
